problem: Conventional VLN needs dense step-by-step instructions, and map-based approaches rely on heavy 2D/3D metric maps. Global planning over a static prior map is also brittle when local connectivity changes at execution time (closed doors, crowded passages).
motivation: Real users give short goal-only commands such as 'take me to the restroom', so agents need structural priors for long-horizon planning. They must also notice when the world deviates from the prior. A lightweight floorplan-level topological map (osmAG) is cheap to obtain and token-efficient for LLMs, but static, so it needs a visual mechanism to detect blockages and update it.
key_idea: Couple LLM planning over a text-based osmAG topological prior with an off-the-shelf VLN executor, and use a fine-tuned VLM Reactive Visual Halting module to detect blockages, prune the blocked passage in osmAG and replan a detour.
insight: A static topological prior lets weaker, single-camera VLN executors handle goal-only instructions: HaltNav's SR drops only from 79.38 (L0-B) to 55.63 (L2-B), a smaller relative decline than the strongest baselines. Explicitly editing the graph cost to infinity, rather than prompting the LLM about obstacles, yields a physically viable detour. Baselines without map guidance collapse under obstacles (mostly under 13% SR at L0-O in simulation, 0% in the real world). No ablation of RVH, GGTD or the synthetic data is reported, so those contributions are supported only by end-to-end comparisons.
method: osmAG prior: text-based Area Graph (rooms as nodes, passages such as doors as edges) converted to a passage-level graph with precomputed A* traversal costs. It supports online node/edge removal or setting cost to infinity, followed by replanning.

Graph-Grounded Task Dispatcher (GGTD): an LLM (Gemini 3 Flash) reads a textual local osmAG sub-graph, the goal instruction and the trajectory history, and outputs door-to-door atomic sub-instructions m_i.
Local executor: an off-the-shelf single-camera VLN policy (InternVLA-N1), agnostic to the global map, maps egocentric observation and sub-instruction to discrete actions.

Reactive Visual Halting (RVH): a termination function combining bottom-up collision accumulation (sum of collision flags over a window of size k ≥ τ_c) with top-down MLLM traversability judgment (Qwen2.5-VL-7B) on the egocentric image and sub-instruction.
Dynamic topology belief update: when a top-down halt confirms a blockage, the traversal cost C(p_i,p_j) is set to infinity, and A* replans on the updated passage graph.

Failure-injection data synthesis: a physics-based engine injects 3D obstacles at bottlenecks in Habitat trajectories, and a generative engine uses diffusion inpainting on real RGB images to create obstructed scenes. These hard negatives are used for LoRA SFT of the MLLM on halt/no-halt decisions.

setting.backbone: Gemini 3 Flash (GGTD, frozen) + Qwen2.5-VL-7B (RVH, LoRA fine-tuned) + InternVLA-N1 (VLN executor, off-the-shelf)
setting.training_data: RVH is fine-tuned on synthetic halt/no-halt data: Habitat-simulated obstacle injection plus diffusion-inpainted real navigation images (scale not given). GGTD and executor are used off the shelf.
setting.observation: monocular egocentric RGB (single camera; Fetch uses an RGB-D D435) plus collision flag and text osmAG
setting.action_space: discrete low-level actions (move forward, turn left, turn right) from the VLN policy
setting.privileged: osmAG map of the environment (prior topological map) given at test time; collision indicator

numbers_note: All results are on the authors' custom benchmark (not a canonical one). SPL is printed as a 0-1 fraction. Tables cover B (standard) and O (obstacle) settings, with Drop and Delta columns omitted here. The real-world table has only L0 and L2.
results: HaltNav is the most robust under obstacle injection, reaching SR 50.00 (L0-O) and 31.25 (L2-O) in simulation versus at most 37.50 for the best baseline (StreamVLN at L0-O). OmniNav has higher standard-setting SR at L0 and L1 (90.63 and 80.63) but collapses to 12.50 and 18.75 under obstacles. On a real Fetch robot, HaltNav gets 56.66 (L0-O) and 46.66 (L2-O) SR while StreamVLN and InternVLA-N1 both get 0.
limitations: Small, custom evaluation: 5 HM3D scenes, only 16 obstacle tasks, and 15 or so real-world trials per condition; no ablations of RVH, GGTD or the synthetic data.
Relies on an available, accurate osmAG prior and a collision signal, and depends on a proprietary LLM (Gemini 3 Flash); standard-setting SR still trails OmniNav at L0 and L1.
Evaluation is on a self-built benchmark, so comparability to standard VLN benchmarks is limited; the data set is not yet released.
